title: Mr Walter Alexander Monteiro vs Mrs Kripalatha Benedicta Lobo on 14 September, 2012

paragraphs.text:
1




 IN THE HIGH COURT OF KARNATAKA AT BANGALORE

 DATED THIS THE 14TH DAY OF SEPTEMBER 2012
 BEFORE

THE HON'BLE MR.JUSTICE MOHAN SHANTANAGOUDAR

 WRIT PETITION NO.27486 OF 2012 (GM-FC)

BETWEEN:

MR. WALTER ALEXANDER MONTEIRO,
AGED ABOUT 51 YEARS,
SON OF FRANCIS MONTEIRO,
RESIDING AT PANNADKA,
KALLIGE VILLAGE,
BANTWAL TALUK, D.K., ... PETITIONER

(BY SRI.NISHIT KUMAR SHETTY, ADVOCATE)

AND:

MRS. KRIPALATHA BENEDICTA LOBO,
@ BENEDICTA ANNA LOBO,
AGED ABOUT 40 YEARS,
WIFE OF WALTER MONTEIRO,
RESIDING AT C-1, DUKES MANOR,
MATADAKANI ROAD,
URVA MARKET,
MANGALORE ... RESPONDENT

(BY SRI.M. SUDHAKAR PAI, ADVOCATE)

 THIS WRIT PETITION IS FILED UNDER ARTICLE 226 
AND 227 OF CONSTITUTION OF INDIA PRAYING TO QUASH
THE ORDER ANNEXURE - A, DATED 28.07.2012 MADE ON
I.A. NO.1 IN M.C. NO.10/2012 PENDING BEFORE THE COURT
OF SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND JMFC, BANTWAL, D.K.

 THIS WRIT PETITION COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS
DAY, COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 2




 ORDER

By the impugned order, the Court below has allowed

the application for amendment filed by the respondent

herein. The records reveal that the petitioner is the

husband of the respondent. However, it seems disputes

have arisen between the parties, hence they decided to live

apart and consequently, they jointly filed MC No.10/2012

before the jurisdictional Court under Section 10(A) of the

Indian Divorce Act, 1869 praying for dissolution of the

marriage by mutual consent by a decree of divorce. During

the pendency of the said matter, again it seems that the

disputes have aggravated between the parties and

ultimately, the respondent herein having felt that no

useful purpose will be served in continuing the divorce

petition filed under Section 10(A) of Indian Divorce Act,

1869, sought to get itself converted as the one filed under

 Section 10 of Indian Divorce Act, 1869. According to the

respondent, since the differences have started mounting

even after filing the consent divorce petition, the petitioner
 3




herein started misbehaving with her and hence she felt

that the petitioner will not give his consent for divorce.

2. It is the case of the petitioner herein that the

respondent has misused the funds of the petitioner to

certain extent and that false cases are being filed by her

against him either under section 498 of IPC etc.,

3. From the above, it is clear that, the parties have

reconciled themselves to come to the conclusion that

consent divorce petition is not solution inasmuch as one

of the parties is not ready for giving consent for divorce,

i.e., petitioner is not ready to give consent for divorce in

view of fresh allegation.

4. Sri. Nishit Kumar Shetty, learned counsel for the

petitioner submits that the adequate opportunities of

being heard are not given to the petitioner before passing

the impugned order, inasmuch as on the date, on which

the impugned order is passed, the father of the counsel for

the petitioner before the Court below was unwell and

Court below has not adjourned the matter on that day. It
 4




is further submitted by him that immediately on the next

day the father of the petitioner's advocate before the Court

below expired.

5. Even if the petitioner were to be heard before the

Court below, the result would be the same. Moreover there

is nothing on record to show that the adjournment is

sought for before the Court below on 28.07.2012. Hence,

the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner

that adjournment was sought for and same was refused

cannot be accepted. In view of the fact and circumstances,

in my considered opinion, the Court below is justified in

converting the petition as the one under Section 10 of the

Indian Divorce Act, 1869 by transposing the petitioner

herein as contesting respondent.

6. It is to be noted here itself that the evidence of the

respondent is already recorded by the Court below fully.

Now, the matter is posted for recording the evidence of the

petitioner herein. Hence, no interference is called for on

that ground also.
Accordingly, the writ petition stands dismissed.
